name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Upright Row
research: Left arm works, right hand grips a post (same post and post-arm as single_arm_dumbbell_lateral_raise: fist at world (-0.735, -0.246, 1.246)). Torso frame, upper arm 0.27 m, forearm+hand 0.33 m, left shoulder (0.22, 0, 0). START: elev 25 plane 90 -> du (0, 0.423, -0.906), elbow (0.22, 0.114, -0.245); forearm (0, 0.196, -0.981) -> fist (0.22, 0.179, -0.569) = world (0.22, -0.20, 0.87): dumbbell (handle across, palm to body, axis -x) in front of the thigh, back plate edge about 0.11 m in front of the hip line, so it clears the thigh (thigh front about -0.09). Elbow bend 14 deg. END: elev 80 plane 30 -> du (0.853, 0.492, -0.174), elbow (0.450, 0.133, -0.047) = just under shoulder height; target fist (0.16, 0.15, -0.20) -> forearm (-0.884, 0.052, -0.466) (world y flipped in fore_world), fist about world (0.16, -0.17, 1.24) = lower chest; elbow bend 130 deg, elbow above and outside the hand (elbow leads). Handle slanted (axis -0.82, 0, 0.57): a square-to-forearm handle would stand near-vertical; this keeps it mostly level with ~27 deg wrist deviation (check measure_wrist). Sources: S1 McAllister 2013 (delt + trap rise with wide grip), S2 Les Mills 2024 (elbow no higher than shoulder, weight to the lower ribs). Facts: research/single_arm_dumbbell_upright_row.json.
